name: IOD-Video
description: We endeavor on a rarely explored task named Insubstantial Object Detection (IOD), which aims to localize the object with following characteristics: (1) amorphous shape with indistinct boundary; (2) similarity to surroundings; (3) absence in color. Accordingly, it is far more challenging to distinguish insubstantial objects in a single static frame and the collaborative representation of spatial and temporal information is crucial. Thus, we construct an IOD-Video dataset comprised of 600 videos (141,017 frames) covering various distances, sizes, visibility, and scenes captured by different spectral ranges. In addition, we develop a spatio-temporal aggregation framework for IOD, in which different backbones are deployed and a spatio-temporal aggregation loss (STAloss) is elaborately designed to leverage the consistency along the time axis. Experiments conducted on IOD-Video dataset demonstrate that spatio-temporal aggregation can significantly improve the performance of IOD. We hope our work will attract further researches into this valuable yet challenging task. The code will be available at: \url{https://github.com/CalayZhou/IOD-Video}.
evaluation_method: Object-detection metrics such as mean Average Precision (mAP) and IoU-based F1 / precision-recall computed over video frames and spatio-temporal tubes
general_score_metric: mean Average Precision (mAP) over annotated frames / sequences
reputation: A recent, specialized dataset for a challenging, rarely-studied detection problem; adoption is limited but of interest to researchers in video and challenging object detection.
notes: Relatively small, domain-specific dataset (600 videos); class imbalance and subtle visual cues increase difficulty; results may not generalize to standard object-detection benchmarks; novel task definition with limited external benchmarks for comparison.
